title: Checkout identity survives an rm -rf and re-clone on an inode-reusing filesystem
description: Found by the Opus review of opum-ai/ward-cli#237 (WCLI-99, APPROVE, finding 1, MEDIUM, product). A checkout is identified only by (root, device, inode): src/adapters/checkout.ts builds the identity, findBinding matches on it in src/domain/vault-state.ts, profile approvals match the same tuple, and unregister.ts and reporting.ts match it too. On a filesystem that reuses a freed inode, a checkout deleted with rm -rf and re-cloned at the same path gets the same identity and silently inherits the old binding and every profile approval. That breaks spec section 7.1, which requires a new clone to be handled explicitly, and the comment in vault-state.ts claims exactly that guarantee. Evidence: the hosted ext4 runner in #237 reproduced it (project-binding T10, now moved aside in the test so it no longer reuses the inode). APFS rarely reuses inode numbers, so the macOS preview is mostly unaffected. ADR 0004 commits to Linux (WCLI-21) and Windows (WCLI-22), so this blocks the Linux T26 run. Needs a design decision from the operator via opum-doc (what else identifies a clone: a creation time, a nonce written into .ward at registration, or the .git directory identity) before it is built.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A decision on what identifies a checkout beyond (root, device, inode) is recorded by opum-doc and as an ADR here

On a filesystem that reuses a freed inode, rm -rf of a registered checkout and a re-clone at the same path is treated as a new checkout: no inherited binding and no inherited profile approval, with a test that does not move the old directory aside
WCLI-21 lists this task as a dependency of its T26 run

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-11-03 to DEC-255 (a2)(4) and (a6), as relayed verbatim by the leader (record: opum-doc, DEC-255 outcome (a6), opum-ai/opum-doc#1597). ADR 0026 names both, supersedes the identity part of ADR 0005 and amends ADR 0023 (the supersede/amend banners on 0005 and 0023 were left out because the shared agent-profile budgets in .lore/agents were already at their limit; 0026's Status names both).

What changed: sameCheckout in src/domain/vault-state.ts now requires root, device, inode AND a present, equal checkoutId; findBinding, isApprovalFor (profile approvals), unregister's belongsTo and withoutBinding, and doctor's stale-approval probe all go through it or compare the nonce. checkoutId is the one optional key on binding and approval records (reader and serializer; absent is omitted, never null; vaultStateFormatVersion stays 1). src/adapters/checkout.ts reads and, after an approved registration only, creates $GIT_DIR/ward/checkout-id (exclusive create, 0600, refusing links; a .git file's gitdir: line read as one bounded 4 KiB line, relative paths against the .git file's directory, realpath, existing directory; GIT_DIR env never read). A git directory that cannot be resolved or written refuses registration with the new catalog code checkout_identity_unavailable. initProject takes a bindCheckout port, wired in src/cli/main.ts.

Evidence: bun run check green, 1172 pass. test/checkout-identity.test.ts pins identical (root, device, inode) with another nonce as a new checkout for bindings and approvals, the optional-key reader and serializer, and the file rules; test/project-binding.test.ts adds an rm -rf and re-clone at the same path (no move aside). Mutation: making sameCheckout ignore the nonce turns the two domain cases red. On APFS the e2e re-clone case still gets a different inode, so it stays green under that mutation; the nonce guarantee is carried by the domain cases, not by the platform's inode behaviour. Not measured: a filesystem that actually reuses the inode (Linux T26 is the first such run; this task is not a flip gate).

Consequences carried for the next release (release path not edited): the release notes of the next release need one line, "a vault written by this version carries a new optional record key, so a 0.1.1 binary refuses it as malformed; downgrade to 0.1.1 is unsupported" (DEC-255 a6 Q1). Existing 0.1.1 bindings and approvals read as unbound and stay in the vault inert; a legacy binding cannot be unregistered from its checkout. The existing profile-approval re-approval filter does not replace a legacy approval (it has no nonce), so it remains inert beside the new one.
